traditional: the Sun square Mars: a hard contact. Vitality, authority, and recognition works against action, conflict, and heat — obstruction, friction, and strained outcomes in these areas.
modern: Identity meets drive and aggression. Energy, assertion, and the will to act become central to the sense of self. Psychologically the square is inner tension to integrate: Rejected aggression gets projected outward or erupts as a short fuse, often with defiance of authority. The energy has to be learned and channeled rather than cut off. The growth is owning both sides instead of splitting them.

cyclic.waxing: Crisis of action: take conscious hold and build a durable form for selfhood against drive, or be thrown off course.
cyclic.waning: Crisis of meaning: break down the selfhood/drive form that has outlived its purpose and reorient toward the next cycle.

business: Friction in this area. Initiative and drive; the cost is friction with authority and a tendency to force things.
shadow: Egotism and needing to be the center collides with anger and recklessness; forcing or splitting it instead of working it through.
arcApplying: Friction builds toward a forced adjustment.
arcSeparating: The crisis passes; what was restructured settles.

readerCopy.body: A director moves the date up and the team pushes back in the same email thread. Management calls the deadline necessary, while the people responsible for delivery point to missing staff, unfinished work, and promises already made elsewhere. The Sun treats the order as settled, while Mars refuses to hide the anger or physical cost of carrying it out. The square turns the schedule into a direct test of whether authority can still force cooperation. The date may hold, but every rushed mistake becomes part of the argument leadership tried to close.
